verses.text: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
A man with a skin disease came up, bowed before him, and said, “Lord, if you’re willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus reached out and touched him. “I am willing,” he said. “Be made clean.” The man was cleansed from his disease right away.
Then Jesus told him, “Make sure you don’t tell anyone. Go show yourself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded as proof to them.”
When Jesus entered Capernaum, a Roman army officer came to him, asking for help.
“Lord, my servant is lying paralyzed at home and suffering terribly,” he said.
Jesus told him, “I’ll come and heal him.”
The officer answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy to have you come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
I’m also a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard this, he was amazed. He told those following him, “I’m telling you the truth: I haven’t found faith like this anywhere in Israel.
I tell you that many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven.
But the kingdom’s own children will be thrown into the darkness outside, where people will weep and grind their teeth.”
Then Jesus said to the officer, “Go. It will happen just as you believed.” The servant was healed at that very moment.
When Jesus went to Peter’s home, he saw Peter’s mother-in-law lying sick with a fever.
Jesus touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
That evening people brought him many who were possessed by demons. He drove the spirits out with a word and healed everyone who was sick.
This fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah had spoken: “He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.”
When Jesus saw the crowds around him, he ordered that they cross to the other side of the lake.
A scribe came to him and said, “Teacher, I’ll follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to rest his head.”
Another disciple said to him, “Lord, let me go bury my father first.”
But Jesus told him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
Jesus got into a boat, and his disciples followed him.
A violent storm suddenly came up on the lake. Waves swept over the boat, but Jesus was asleep.
The disciples woke him and said, “Lord, save us! We’re going to die!”
He said to them, “Why are you afraid, you who have so little faith?” Then he stood up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and everything became calm.
The men were amazed and said, “What kind of man is this? Even the wind and sea obey him!”
When Jesus reached the other side in the region of the Gergesenes, two men possessed by demons met him. They came out of the tombs and were so violent that nobody could pass that way.
They shouted, “What do you want with us, Son of God? Have you come to torture us before the appointed time?”
A large herd of pigs was feeding some distance away.
The demons begged him, “If you’re driving us out, send us into that herd of pigs.”
He told them, “Go!” They came out and went into the pigs. Then the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
The men tending the pigs ran into the town and told everyone what had happened, including what happened to the demon-possessed men.
The whole town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their region.
